choices.term: Ἐλεημοσύναις γὰρ καὶ πίστεσιν ἀποκαθαίρονται ἁμαρτίαι
choices.english: For almsgiving and faith cleanse sins
choices.why: Direct rendering of causal clause with accusative objects of cleansing; ἀποκαθαίρονται is passive present indicative third plural matching compound subject

choices.term: Μάθετε γὰρ ἀπ' ἐμοῦ, φησίν, ὅτι πραΰς εἰμι καὶ ταπεινὸς τῇ καρδίᾳ
choices.english: Learn from me, for I am meek and lowly in heart
choices.why: Imperative Μαθέτε preserved as direct address; γὰρ as explanatory 'for'; ὅτι introduces quoted speech; dative τῇ καρδίᾳ as 'in heart' per Biblical usage
rejected: Learn of me that I am meek and humble of heart

choices.term: Κἂν ἔχω γὰρ πίστιν, ὥστε ὄρη μεθιστάναι, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, οὐθέν εἰμι
choices.english: For if I have faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing
choices.why: Κἂν = καὶ ἐν for concessive 'even if'; ὥστε with infinitive expresses purpose/result; οὐθέν strengthened negation; matches 1 Cor 13:2 wording

pass_a_gloss: For almsgiving and faith cleanse sins; zealous is meekness, but without humility it cannot produce a royal character; 'Learn from me, for I am meek and lowly in heart'; good is faith, even as its smallest grain can move mountains, but without love it is vain and excessive; 'For if I have faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing'; therefore let us beloved, pursue these virtues, that we may
pass_b_english: Almsgiving and faith work together to cleanse sins.
Meekness is a desirable trait, but it cannot produce a royal character without humility.
As Jesus taught, we should learn from him, because he is meek and lowly in heart (Matthew 11:29).
Faith, even in small amounts, has the power to move mountains, but without love, it becomes empty and excessive.
The apostle Paul emphasized this point, saying that even if we have faith that can move mountains, but do not have love, we are nothing (1 Corinthians 13:2).
Therefore, let us strive to pursue these virtues, that we may...
source_text:
«Ἐλεημοσύναις γὰρ καὶ πίστεσιν ἀποκαθαίρονται ἁμαρτίαι.» Ζηλωτὸν ἡ πραότης,
ἀλλὰ χωρὶς τῆς ταπεινώσεως βασιλικὸν ἀποτελέσαι χαρακτῆρα οὐ δύναται·
«Μάθετε γὰρ ἀπ' ἐμοῦ, φησίν, ὅτι πραΰς εἰμι καὶ ταπεινὸς τῇ καρδίᾳ.» Καλὸν ἡ πίστις
ὡς καὶ τὸ βραχύτατον αὐτῆς ὄρη δύνασθαι μεθιστᾶν, ἀλλὰ χωρὶς ἀγάπης εἰκαία καὶ
περιττὴ καθέστηκεν· «Κἂν ἔχω γὰρ πίστιν», φησίν, «ὥστε ὄρη μεθιστάναι, ἀγάπην δὲ
μὴ ἔχω, οὐθέν εἰμι.» Σπουδάσωμεν οὖν, ἀγαπητοί, τὰς ἀρετὰς ταύτας μετελθεῖν, ἵνα
